artworks.title: Venus and Adonis
artworks.description: Veronese's Prado canvas shows Venus clinging to Adonis as he rises for the hunt — the doomed youth already half-turned toward the boar that will kill him. Soft Venetian colour wraps a myth of love that cannot hold him.

artworks.title: The Death of Adonis
artworks.description: Rubens stages the aftermath in the Israel Museum: Venus rushes to the fallen Adonis while the fatal boar still lurks in the landscape — grief and blood painted with Baroque urgency.

artworks.title: Venus, Adonis and Cupid
artworks.description: Carracci's Prado painting freezes a quieter moment: Venus and Adonis at rest with Cupid nearby, before the hunt. Classical bodies and cool light make the coming death feel almost inevitable.

artworks.title: Death of Adonis
artworks.description: An early High Renaissance lament in the Uffizi: Venus and her companions gather around Adonis's corpse as the landscape opens behind them — the dying beloved as Venetian tragedy.

popCulture.title: Venus and Adonis
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: Shakespeare's narrative poem made Adonis the reluctant beloved of Venus — the boar's victim as Elizabethan erotic elegy.

popCulture.title: Adonis
popCulture.description: English still calls a strikingly handsome man an Adonis — the dying beloved turned into a compliment.

popCulture.title: Adonis (plant)
popCulture.description: The anemone-like Adonis flower keeps his blood in the spring garden — the youth's wound as a genus of buttercups.
